questions.question: Why must water from a dam be cleaned before we drink it, and where is it cleaned?
questions.expected_answer: Dam water may look clean, but it contains mud, tiny bits of plants and germs from animals and people, which can cause diseases. It is carried by pipes to a water treatment works, also called a purification plant, where it is cleaned.

questions.question: Name and explain the steps used to clean water at a treatment works.
questions.expected_answer: Screening: screens catch sticks, leaves and rubbish. Adding chemicals: tiny bits of dirt stick together into clumps called flocs. Settling: the clumps sink to the bottom of still tanks. Filtering: the water trickles through sand and gravel to remove tiny bits. Disinfection: chlorine kills germs. Scientists test the water throughout.

questions.question: How does clean water get from the treatment works to your tap, and what happens to it after you use it?
questions.expected_answer: Pumps push the clean water through big pipes to reservoirs, which are closed tanks often on hills. Gravity makes it flow down through smaller pipes to homes and taps, and a meter measures how much is used. After use, it flows down drains into sewer pipes to a wastewater treatment works, where it is cleaned and returned to a river.
